data.name: Giosue
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew name 'Yehoshua', meaning 'God will give'. In the Bible, Joshua was the successor of Moses, leading the Israelites into the promised land.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolic of God's guidance and provision.

in_hebrew.name: ג'ושוע
in_hebrew.meaning: אין שם הפרטי שמקורו בעברית. מקורו בנביא העברי ישוע.
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ג'ושוע הוא שם הנביא הבורא. ישוע (ישוע) הוא שם יחידי של נביא ישראלי, בנו של יהושע הצדיק. השם נמצא באופן יחידי בארץ-ישראל. חלק מההיסטוריונים העריכו שהשם ישוע, שפירושו 'יושב', חוזר ומתייחס לבני ישראל, וכי ישוע מהווה דוגמא לאיש שתפקד כפרנס, ובעל תפקיד בבית דין.

in_greek.name: Γιόσου
in_greek.meaning: ονομασιακός της εβραϊκής προέλευσης. Μετονομασία του Ιησού
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Γίουσεως (Ιωσήφ) ήταν ο πατέρας του Ιησού και ο αντίθετος του τούτου. Ο Ιησούς ονομάστηκε για να τον διακρίνουμε από τον Γίουσεως. Η ονομασία του Ιησούς είναι ελληνική και προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή ονομασία του Γίουσεως.

in_latin.name: Giosue
in_latin.meaning: nominis Hebraici originis. Iosephus, pater Iesu
in_latin.long_meaning: Giosue, nomine Iosephi, pater Iesu Christi. Iosephus, nomine Hebraico, significat 'additus' aut 'additus Deus'. Nomen Iosephi, pater Iesu, in Genesi 41, 50-53 et in Matthaeo 1, 16 apparit.

in_english.name: Giosue
in_english.meaning: name of Hebrew origin. Joseph, father of Jesus
in_english.long_meaning: Giosue is the name of Joseph, the father of Jesus Christ. Joseph is a name of Hebrew origin, meaning 'addition' or 'added by God'. The name Joseph, father of Jesus, appears in Genesis 41, 50-53 and in Matthew 1, 16.

biblical_reference.note: Name of Joseph, father of Jesus Christ, appears in Genesis and Gospels.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Giosue" (pronounced "JO-zoo-eh") is an Italian variation of the Hebrew name "Joshua". In Italian culture, the name "Giosue" has been well-known thanks to its biblical associations and the significant historical figure it represents. Giosue is seen as a name suggesting strength, courage, and leadership, as in the story of the original Joshua, who led the Israelites to conquer the promised land. The name is also associated with Italian art, literature, and folklore, and has been used in various Italian works, from operas to novels.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Giosue" maintains its rich spiritual significance, derived from its original Hebrew roots. The name 'Yehoshua' in Hebrew signifies 'God will give'. This spiritual meaning emphasizes faith, trust, and reliance on God's guidance in one's life journey. In the Judeo-Christian tradition, Joshua was a strong leader who trusted in God's promises, and following his example can inspire those bearing the name to possess a deep sense of faith and allegiance to the Divine Providence.

historical_references.reference: Giosue (Joshua) was the successor of Moses, leading the Israelites to the Promised Land after the Exodus from Egypt.
Giosue Bellini, an Italian painter of the Quattrocento period, was known for his religious paintings, including 'The Feast of the Gods' and 'The Virgin and Child with St. George'.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name 'Giosue' (Joshua in English) is often associated with Italian culture, biblical figures, and historical context. In the Italian tourism industry, there are numerous sites dedicated to the history of Giosue, such as the Temple of Joshua in Palermo, Sicily. In literature and media, Giosue is a popular character in novels, films, and television shows that explore the religious and historical significance of the biblical figure. Within the Catholic community, Giosue is celebrated in various events and festivals, particularly during the Feast of Saint Joshua held annually on March 11.

name_in_real_life.story: Hannah Giosue from New York, United States embodies the meaning of Giosue - "God will give". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Giosue, meaning "God is salvation," symbolizes the belief in divine intervention and deliverance from troubles in one's life. It is a reminder of God's promise to save and protect His children, instilling faith and trust in the Almighty.
